stem:
Scores of a Hifz e Quran test were grouped into the following frequency distribution.
| scores | $41-50$ | $51-60$ | $61-70$ | $71-80$ | $81-90$ | $91-100$ |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| $f$ | 3 | 17 | 20 | 30 | 18 | 2 |
Draw a cumulative frequency table and cumulative frequency curve (ogive) and tell:
a) How many boys appeared in the test?
b) What is median score?
c) How many boys scored under median?
d) How many boys fell in first decile?
e) How many boys fell in $30^{\text{th}}$ percentile?
f) If excellence award is to be given to boys falling in $100^{\text{th}}$ percentile, how many boys got excellence award?
keyPoints: ["Median splits ninety observations at forty-five","Cross-check the positional class against the cumulative column"]
modelAnswer:
Cumulative counts: $3,20,40,70,88,90$.
a. Ninety boys appeared.
b. Median position $45$ lies in $70.5-80.5$: median $=70.5+\frac{5}{30}(45-40)\approx71.33$.
c. Forty-five boys scored under the median by definition.
d. First-decile band runs up to $D_{1}=50.5+\frac{5}{17}(9-3)\approx52.26$, containing about nine boys.
e. Thirtieth percentile: $30$ boys lie below it ($P_{30}\approx62.25$).
f. The hundredth percentile equals the single highest score; grouped data cannot isolate how
many boys share that exact mark, so the award count stays undetermined rather than guessed.

The masses measured to the nearest kg of 50 cubs are shown below:
| Mass (kg) | $60-64$ | $65-69$ | $70-74$ | $75-79$ | $80-84$ | $85-89$ |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| $f$ | 2 | 6 | 12 | 14 | 10 | 6 |
(i) Construct a cumulative frequency table
(ii) Construct a cumulative frequency polygon and estimate number of cubs above 77 kg.
(iii) Construct a cumulative frequency curve and estimate number of cubs above 77 kg.
(iv) Compare the results of (ii) & (iii)
keyPoints: ["Interpolate inside the class holding the target value","Cross-check the positional class against the cumulative column"]
modelAnswer:
i. Cumulative counts: $2,8,20,34,44,50$.
ii. Polygon estimate: interpolating inside $74.5-79.5$ gives
$20+14\times\frac{77-74.5}{5}=27$, so about $50-27=23$ cubs exceed seventy-seven kg.
iii. The smooth ogive crosses the same class interval and yields essentially the same reading,
about twenty-three cubs above seventy-seven kg.
iv. Both constructions agree because both interpolate linearly within the same class;
the curve merely smooths the polygon's corners.

b. What is type of correlation?
c. What conclusion can be drawn from this?
keyPoints: ["Five-number summaries fix every box-plot hinge","Cross-check the positional class against the cumulative column"]
modelAnswer:
Box plots place five hinges each on a common scale.
Mass: min $1100$, $Q_{1}1200$, median $1500$, $Q_{3}1700$, max $2000$, so IQR $=500$ kg.

b. Heavier cars pair with lower efficiency: negative correlation.
c. Conclusion: fuel economy falls as vehicle mass rises.

stem:
Khola wants to forecast the temperature for the next week for Jhelum and Indiana. She has the history of a week for both of the cities as given:
Jhelum:
| Temperature(F°) | 96-100 | 101-105 | 106-110 | 111-115 |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| No. of days | 2 | 3 | 1 | 1 |
Indiana:
| Temperature(F°) | 51-60 | 61-70 | 71-80 | 81-90 |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| No. of days | 3 | 1 | 2 | 1 |
Help her to find:
i. Mean of both data sets.
ii. Variance of both datasets
Also comment on the possible predictions for next week temperature for both cities. (Hint: In weather forecasting, variance is used to measure the spread or uncertainty in temperature predictions. A higher variance indicates a wider range of possible temperatures, making it more challenging to predict the exact temperature.)
keyPoints: ["Smaller variance supports bolder forecasts","Cross-check the positional class against the cumulative column"]
modelAnswer:
Jhelum midpoints $98,103,108,113$, days $2,3,1,1$: mean $\approx103.71^{\circ}$F;
variance $\approx24.5$. Indiana midpoints $55.5,65.5,75.5,85.5$, days $3,1,2,1$:
mean $\approx66.93^{\circ}$F; variance $\approx126.5$.
Prediction: Jhelum should stay near one hundred four degrees with little swing, while Indiana
sits cooler but with a much wider spread, so its weekly forecast carries more uncertainty.
sectionLabel: Comparison of 2 Data Sets using Mean and Standard Deviation

stem: What is the probability of a patient testing positive for a disease with either Test A or Test B, given that the probability of testing positive with Test A is 0.3 and the probability of testing positive with Test B is 0.4, and the tests are independent?
keyPoints: ["Independence multiplies the joint probability","Cross-check the positional class against the cumulative column"]

$P(A \cup B)=0.3+0.4-(0.3)(0.4)=0.58$.

stem: Musaab picked a card randomly from a box containing cards bearing numbers 1, 2 and 3. He then replaced and picked another after well shuffling. He found product of two numbers he got in 2 trials. Draw the possibility diagram of this experiment and find probability of getting an even product.
keyPoints: ["Replacement keeps all nine outcomes equally likely","Cross-check the positional class against the cumulative column"]
modelAnswer:
Possibility diagram: rows for first pick $1,2,3$ and columns for second pick $1,2,3$
give nine ordered outcomes whose products are
$1,2,3;\ 2,4,6;\ 3,6,9$.
Even products occur five times out of nine: $P(\text{even})=\frac{5}{9}$.
